peak_vram_measurement_note: The Modal parent Function process's torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated/reserved calls returned 0.0/0.0 in both attempts because the parent process never itself held the model -- vLLM's tensor-parallel worker subprocesses (Worker_TP0, Worker_TP1) did. A value genuinely observed from the wrong process is not honest evidence of the real peak_allocated/peak_reserved magnitude, so these fields are recorded NOT_CAPTURED rather than the misleading 0.0. See runtime_worker_memory below for genuine, differently-measured worker-level evidence from vLLM's own self-reported log accounting -- this is why this manifest's NOT_CAPTURED is accepted for a QUALIFIED result under the schema's alternate-evidence rule.

runtime_worker_memory.note: Values taken verbatim from the canonical attempt-2 raw execution log (Worker_TP0 and Worker_TP1 both reported identically): 'Actual usage is 57.45 GiB for consumed memory (weights + non-torch), 0.54 GiB for peak activation, and 0.08 GiB for CUDAGraph memory... Current kv cache memory in use is 60.84 GiB.' (gpu_worker.py:860). Not invented, not reinterpreted -- these are vLLM's own self-reported numbers, using vLLM's own terminology (consumed/activation/CUDAGraph/kv-cache), which is a genuinely different accounting methodology from torch.cuda's peak_allocated/peak_reserved caching-allocator semantics and is not force-fit into those two fields.

runtime_loaded_weight_files_note: Repository fact (weight_file_shards=3, from model.safetensors.index.json's weight_map, REPOSITORY_VERIFIED) vs. runtime-observed fact (runtime_loaded_weight_files=7, OBSERVED_LIVE): the repository publishes BOTH a 3-shard HF-transformers-style sharded-index layout (model-0000X-of-00003.safetensors) AND a separate native 7-file 'consolidated*.safetensors' checkpoint format. vLLM's loader selected the 7-file consolidated format for both attempts ('Parse safetensors files: 0/7'...'7/7', 'Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 7/7', 'Inferred from consolidated*.safetensors files torch.bfloat16 dtype'). Both facts are true and are not conflated: weight_file_shards records what the repository's own index declares; runtime_loaded_weight_files records what this specific runtime actually read off disk.
